questions.prompt: The same request costs less when repeated in a warm session than the first time. What is the mechanism?
options: The second request is shorter because the model remembers and compresses your earlier wording
Previously processed context is served from the prompt cache at a reduced rate, and the cache expires on a TTL
Subscriptions discount the second identical request as a loyalty repeat
The agent reuses the earlier tool results instead of re-running the tools
questions.explanation: The prompt cache is what makes a re-send cheaper: content already processed is reused at a reduced rate, until a TTL expires and the next request pays full price again. Option A describes a memory behaviour the model does not have — it re-sends the same bytes every time. Option D confuses the model-side cache with the tool layer; tool results are still re-sent either way.

questions.prompt: You have a small change to make in a 200,000-token repo. Which ask is most likely to be both fast and cheap?
options: Investigate the repo to understand how this area works before making the change
Change the named constant on the line named, then run the named test
Refactor the surrounding module so the change fits the existing conventions
Search for every usage of the constant across the repo, read each match's context, and update them consistently
questions.explanation: Cost and latency both scale with round trips, and each round trip re-sends the whole context. Naming the file and the test collapses the task to one or two round trips. Option A spends a full investigation on a change you could have described precisely. Option D is genuinely thorough, which is exactly why it is the most expensive — and for a single constant it is wasted effort.

questions.prompt: An agent call has been running four minutes with no output. You open the terminal and find nothing obviously stuck. What is the most useful next move?
options: Restart the session — a stall this long always means a dead agent
Classify the stall: did it stop at a usage-limit message, at your own long-running command, or at the model's first token
Switch to a smaller model to get past the stall
Add more detail to the prompt so the model has more to work with
questions.explanation: The three stalls have different signatures and different fixes, and only one is yours to fix — a limit message, your own hanging test suite, or a genuinely slow first token are distinguishable in the transcript. Option A destroys the work for a problem that may be a five-second wait. Option C changes capability, which is not what latency is. Option D adds context to a request that has not started responding, so it changes nothing.
